espn-604011.headline: Italy beat England in March. Now they play for 11th
beats: Six pool games in, Italy have no wins. This is the 11th-place final, at Allianz Stadium in London, against the Fiji side that beat them in Udine on 21 November.
Italy led that one 13-7 at half-time and lost 16-21. Fiji scored twice in seven minutes after the break to take their first win of the competition. Il Giornale's verdict was "Crisi vera".
Italy arrive on seven straight losses. A win would lift them above Fiji to 10th in the world, and end the competition with something to show for it.
Their next game is at Scotland in February, in the Six Nations, the tournament where the England win happened. Going back there without a Nations Championship win is a poor thing to carry.

espn-604012.headline: Beat the world champions, play for fifth
beats: Ireland's 20-17 win over South Africa in Dublin left them third in the North, a point behind England. South Africa lost and still made the final. Ireland get Australia at Twickenham in the fifth-place final.

The July meeting in Sydney went 33-31 to Ireland, settled by Thomas Clarkson's late try and Sam Prendergast's conversion. Ben Donaldson then missed a penalty with the final kick that would have won it.

Les Kiss, once Ireland's defence coach and later Ulster's boss, succeeded Joe Schmidt as Australia coach this year. His side reached this game by beating Wales 29-26 in Cardiff, a fortnight after England beat them 45-22.
A win lifts Ireland to third in the world, an odd prize for a play-off for fifth. Their next Test is England at home in February, the side that finished a point ahead of them.

espn-604013.headline: Japan ran Wales close. Then they conceded 145
beats: On 7 November in Cardiff, Japan trailed by seven at half-time, and Wales did not land the decisive try until the 69th minute. Since then Eddie Jones' side have lost 78–15 to England and 67–5 to Scotland, shipping 11 tries at Murrayfield.

Wales beat New Zealand 35–28 and then let Australia come back to win 29–26 in Cardiff. Steve Tandy is set to make changes and give fringe players their chance in the ninth-place final, which says something about how he rates the rematch.
Only a big Japan win moves anything. A margin of 16 or more would lift them above Wales, who would drop to 11th. Their last fortnight makes that a long way from here.
Wales go to France in February. Japan have nothing scheduled, which leaves them a long winter with whatever happens in London.

espn-604014.headline: Beaten by 25, New Zealand need 16 to be No. 1 again
beats: Seven days after England's 37–12 win at Allianz Stadium, the biggest margin they have ever had over New Zealand, the sides meet on the same ground in the third-place final. Second in the North plays second in the South.
New Zealand conceded 35 to Wales and 37 to England in successive weeks. Dave Rennie called his side "miles off" and said he was a "big part of that".
England beat New Zealand 33–19 at home last November and 37–12 at home on 21 November. They managed the second without Tommy Freeman, and Steve Borthwick is hopeful about his fitness.
Win by 16 or more and New Zealand are first in the world again, above South Africa. Lose, and they have until Chile next October to think about it.

espn-604015.headline: Scotland are at home at Twickenham, playing for seventh
beats: Scotland are the home side at Twickenham, in the game that settles seventh place overall. It is the opening act for France and South Africa in the final.

Scotland put 11 tries past Japan, three of them by Liam McConnell, and Tom English wants him let loose on Argentina. Argentina conceded seven tries to France in Paris and had Mayco Vivas sent off for a clearout into Maxime Lamothe's head.

The last two meetings went to the side on the road: Argentina won 33–24 away to Scotland in November 2025, and Scotland won 47–38 in Cordoba in July. Only an Argentina win by 16 or more takes them above Scotland in the world rankings.
Scotland host Italy in February. Argentina's next game is Canada at the World Cup, which is a long time to sit on seventh or eighth.

espn-604016.headline: Two points in Paris, the whole thing in London
beats: France beat South Africa 21–19 in Paris on 13 November. Now the world's top-ranked side get a second go, in the first Nations Championship final, at Allianz Stadium.

South Africa have not won since. They lost 20–17 in Dublin and still finished top of the South, ahead of New Zealand on points difference, thanks to a losing bonus point. France put seven tries past Argentina, 45–17, for a fifth straight win.
Nick Mallett called it "quite fortunate for us" that the final is not against England. France could leave London with more than the trophy: win by 16 or more and they go top of the world rankings.
South Africa's next Test after this is a World Cup pool game in October. A third straight defeat would make for a long wait.
